profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record in San Jose, California, is one of two nearly identical points both named simply "STACK Infrastructure" at this location, most plausibly reflecting a duplicate map entry for the same underlying campus rather than two genuinely separate facilities. This duplication is documented explicitly here rather than silently resolved. That campus, which STACK's own site identifies by the code SVY01, is a 19-acre, four-building site with 100 megawatts of total IT capacity, made up of SVY01A at 9 megawatts across 140,000 square feet, SVY01B at 32 megawatts across 240,000 square feet, SVY01C at 36 megawatts across 350,000 square feet, and SVY01D at 24 megawatts across 300,000 square feet. STACK's own marketing describes the surrounding area as "among the most constrained development regions" within Silicon Valley, reflecting the well-documented land, power, and water constraints facing new data center construction in San Jose and neighboring Santa Clara. STACK, headquartered in Denver, Colorado, reports roughly 8.5 gigawatts of capacity built or under development across 24 global markets company-wide, and describes its overall Silicon Valley market as "3 campuses across 97 acres" totaling 150 megawatts. STACK's own site names and details only two campuses, however, SVY01 at 100 megawatts and SVY02 at 48 megawatts, together totaling 148 megawatts, leaving a small, unexplained gap that most plausibly points to an undisclosed or not-yet-announced third Silicon Valley site rather than to an error in either figure. This discrepancy is noted honestly rather than resolved. No street address, year of completion, or named power utility is disclosed on STACK's public page for SVY01, and tenant identities are not publicly disclosed, consistent with standard industry practice.

reading.body:
This campus in San Jose is attributed to Stack Infrastructure, Incorporated, the formal entity name for STACK Infrastructure, a operator with eleven US facilities already documented in this registry. No individual megawatt figure or building address for this particular San Jose location was found in available sources, so its size cannot be calculated and its ranking reflects only that it ranks below the eleven California facilities with published specifications.

California has 103 mapped data center facilities in OpenStreetMap, of which only eleven have published power capacity figures totaling 365 MW. This San Jose campus is not among those eleven with disclosed specifications, which means its contribution to the state's AI infrastructure capacity is unknown and cannot be compared to peers.

Without published power specifications, this facility cannot be evaluated for its relevance to AI scaling in the region. The state context provided ranks only disclosed capacity, and this campus does not appear in that set.
